thread:
Anya: quick follow-up on the epochal pin serialization RFC — thinking about fallback heuristics when a pinned epoch isn't available. TL;DR: we need clearer precedence rules and a compact on-wire format. Thoughts?

Julian: Agree on both. Main tradeoff is backward-compat vs compact encoding. My preference: keep explicit 'epoch' and 'fallback_chain' fields for control plane visibility, but allow a compact binary header for fast routing. Example human-friendly metadata: { epoch: '2024-09-01T00:00Z', fallback_chain: ['v2', 'v1-shim'] }

Marta: Ops point — we also need lease/affinity windows. If epoch expired, should we auto-fallback to latest compatible or strictly respect tenant pin? I worry about silent drift if we auto-route to latest. We want graceful degradation, not surprising behaviour for customers.

Sam: Proposal for fallback heuristic (simple):
1) If tenant pin exists and now <= epoch + grace_window -> honor pin.
2) If pin expired but fallback_chain provided -> try each in order.
3) If none match -> route to 'compatibility-mode' model and surface a metric + alert.
Example snippet: `pin_policy: { epoch: "2024-09-01T00:00Z", grace_window_s: 86400, fallback_chain: ["v2","v1-shim"] }`

Julian: On-wire format idea: a compact TLV-ish header for fast path parsing: EPOCH(4B) + FLAGS(1B) + HASH(20B). That allows routers to parse and make routing decisions w/o touching JSON blobs. Keep a JSON metadata blob in control-plane for ops. Perf win for high-throughput proxies.

Marta: Ops concern: migration safety. Servers must ignore unknown TLV tags and default to safe behavior. Also we need explicit telemetry when fallback occurs (tenant_id, requested_epoch, served_variant) so we can detect rollouts that silently degrade.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: added metric pin_fallback.v1 to staging metrics stream ~10m ago.

Anya: sounds good. Can we standardize on these fields for the schema: epoch, grace_window_s, fallback_chain[], pin_strict (bool), telemetry_event_name? I'll open a PR for the schema and a tiny migration runbook.

Sam: +1 — also add a small client shim suggestion to prefer explicit pins when provided and to expose a clear opt-out for strict tenants.

Julian: I'll prototype the TLV encoder/decoder and bench it against current JSON header parsing; will post numbers here.

Marta: please add a short ops playbook section: how to debug pin fallbacks, how to force a strict pin, and how to roll back a bad fallback chain.

Anya: action items: PR with schema & examples by EOD, TLV prototype by end of week, ops playbook draft. Thanks all :rocket:
